_about: Plain rewordings of researched ledger entries that quoted a critic's slogan (user, 28 Nov 2026: "look for sentenses slogans and make them normal"; of critics' quotations: yes). Keyed by the entry's summary as the checkers left it; tools/merge_came_with.py and tools/merge_reputation.py apply it last, so a re-merge keeps the plain wording. The speaker, the date and the source are unchanged.

plain.In December 2023 Doug Parr, policy direc: In December 2023 Doug Parr, policy director of Greenpeace UK, said of the £50 million deal that no cultural body should take fossil fuel companies' money in exchange for improving their public image.
plain.In June 2019 Gary Hume, a judge of that: In June 2019 Gary Hume, a judge of that year's BP Portrait Award, wrote to the gallery's director that the art world should stop helping the oil industry improve its public image.
plain.In January 2026, after documents showed: In January 2026, after documents showed BP's role in the museum's STEM academy, Stuart Tannock of UCL said linking the BP brand with STEM education helps the company keep public acceptance of its business.
plain.On 22 December 2014 the First-tier Tribu: On 22 December 2014 the First-tier Tribunal, ordering Tate to disclose BP sponsorship sums, accepted that arts sponsorship can be understood as a way for BP to keep public acceptance of its operations.
plain.An open letter in Mediapart in October 2: An open letter in Mediapart in October 2014, signed by Georges Didi-Huberman, Giorgio Agamben and others, opposed celebrating the foundation's opening. It said such groups use art as a display and their patrons are speculators.
plain.In October 2018 Chris Garrard of Culture: In October 2018 Chris Garrard of Culture Unstained said that by leaving the National Gallery Shell admitted it was a company with a badly damaged reputation that it needed to repair.
plain.Fridays for Future Salzburg staged a die: Fridays for Future Salzburg staged a die-in at the first Jedermann performance in July 2022 with a banner accusing Audi of greenwashing, objecting to Audi as festival sponsor.
plain.In November 2025 Dr Allen Gallagher of t: In November 2025 Dr Allen Gallagher of the University of Bath said deals like JTI's with the British Museum let the tobacco industry, whose products kill, use cultural institutions to improve its public image.
plain.In January 2024 Barry Healy wrote in Red: In January 2024 Barry Healy wrote in Red Spark that Perth artists had ended the public acceptance Chevron gained from the sponsorship. Anthony Collins said a board member told him the festival divested under pressure.
plain.The Fossil Free Louvre campaign against: The Fossil Free Louvre campaign against Total's sponsorship said in 2017 that fossil fuel companies gain an appearance of respectability from their Louvre partnership.
plain.In October 2026 Nicole Regalado of We Ar: In October 2026 Nicole Regalado of We Are UltraViolet said MoMA was helping to repair Leon Black's reputation by keeping him on its board. Protesters near the museum called for his removal.
plain.Greta Thunberg pulled out of the August: Greta Thunberg pulled out of the August 2023 festival over Baillie Gifford's sponsorship. Her statement said the fossil fuel industry's greenwashing, sponsorship of cultural events included, helps it keep public acceptance of its business.
plain.Right Side Of History IRL's petition, si: A 2025 petition by Right Side Of History IRL says IMMA's listing of BNP Paribas as a Freud Circle sponsor makes the bank's practices look acceptable and wants it removed. The partnership ended in 2019.
plain.In November 2023 Julie Forchhammer, co-f: In November 2023 Julie Forchhammer, co-founder of the Norwegian group Klimakultur, said Equinor's sponsorship of the Wonderlab gallery was part of a strategy of using culture to improve the company's image.
plain.In an open letter of 19 February 2014, p: In an open letter of 19 February 2014, participating artists told the Biennale board that their part in the sponsored event added value to the Transfield brand and lent the company cultural standing.
plain.Trustees Jo Foster and Hannah Fry resign: Trustees Jo Foster and Hannah Fry resigned in November 2021 after the museum partnered with Adani Green Energy. Fry wrote in The Times that such ties wrongly suggest fossil fuel companies are doing enough.
plain.Joanna Haigh, former co-director of the: Joanna Haigh, former co-director of the Grantham Institute, told The Art Newspaper in March 2023 the deal was a plain case of greenwashing that let the company gain respectability from its link to the museum.
plain.More than 150 people occupied the museum: More than 150 people occupied the museum in March 2024, days before the gallery opened. Mukti Shah of South Asia Solidarity Group said the museum was helping the corporation present itself as green.
plain.In July 2015 David Aaker, vice chairman: In July 2015 David Aaker, vice chairman of the consultancy Prophet, wrote that the MoMA partnership improves Uniqlo's brand image.
plain.Extinction Rebellion accused ING of \"ar: Extinction Rebellion accused ING of using art to improve its image and campaigned for the Rijksmuseum to break with it. On 1 March 2025 its supporters reserved thousands of museum tickets and stayed away.
plain.In Vienna for the Opera Ball in February: In Vienna for the Opera Ball in February 2023, Jane Fonda said fossil fuel firms give money to museums and operas to win public approval and was sorry to learn OMV sponsors the opera.
plain.Artist Adam Bennett wrote in June 2021 t: Artist Adam Bennett wrote in June 2021 that ten nights of protest readings beside the festival's Woodside Pleasure Garden challenged the public acceptance Woodside gains from the sponsorship.
plain.In June 2026 Matt Roberts, executive dir: In June 2026 Matt Roberts, executive director of the Conservation Council of WA, said Woodside spends heavily to make itself part of the state's cultural life and named the WA Museum among those it funds.
plain.The letter “Kanders Must Go” of April 20: The April 2019 letter “Kanders Must Go”, signed by over 120 scholars and critics, said institutions like the Whitney shield people like Kanders from criticism and called for a debate on art used for reputation.
plain.Asher Gamedze and Mitchel Hunter, in the: Asher Gamedze and Mitchel Hunter, in the Mail & Guardian in April 2018, cited Nathan Kirsh's Magal Security Systems holding and asked whether Black artists at A4 were used to make occupation profits look acceptable.
plain.In January 2020 the academics Delinda Co: In January 2020 the academics Delinda Collier and Marissa Moorman wrote in Africa Is a Country that Dokolo's patronage of African artists and his repatriation efforts improve his public image.
plain.An open letter of 27 May 2026, signed by: An open letter of 27 May 2026, signed by over 100 art professionals including Ali Cherri and Dominique Gonzalez-Foerster, said the Centre Pompidou partnership uses art to improve Hanwha's image and asked for its end.
plain.In January 1991 the Time critic Robert H: In January 1991 the Time critic Robert Hughes called it the most vain museum in America, paid for by Occidental's shareholders, and wrote that Hammer toured his collection worldwide to promote Occidental and himself.
plain.Writing in soL in November 2025, Osman G: Writing in soL in November 2025, Osman Gece named Eczacıbaşı's İKSV among institutions that he said improve the image of big business and produce soft power through culture.
